That does not mean martyring your own family. It means planning like a human being, not a bunker fantasy. Maybe that looks like one extra bag of rice. Maybe it looks like checking on somebody's oxygen backup (and asking them how their family got through the 1973 oil embargo. Elder have wisdom!). Maybe it looks like sharing information calmly and responsibly with trusted friends before rumors do what rumors always do.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/488ce707-535e-4a18-a5f6-fff3411fc121?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* * *
We have to refuse two temptations at once.
The first temptation is **denial**.
"The market will sort it out."
"It can't really happen here."
"Someone would fix it."
That is magical thinking in a nicer outfit.
The second temptation is **nihilism**.
"It's over."
"Nothing matters."
"Just grab what you can."
That is **spiritual surrender** , and it helps no one except predators.
_There is a better lane._
Tell the truth about fragility.
Take practical steps.
Do not panic-buy.
Do not spread nonsense you cannot stand behind.
Do not wait for perfect certainty before doing obviously prudent things.
And do not let fear isolate you from the people right around you.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=3260111&post_id=191131787&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkxMTMxNzg3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzYyMDYyMTcsImV4cCI6MTc3ODc5ODIxNywiaXNzIjoicHViLTMyNjAxMTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.jbbHFutACraQMg6X75MN81Y2WarG-29hn2lmBfFxtCE)
* * *
I have been thinking for most of my life about how much of modern life depends on systems most people never chose and cannot control. That is part of why I keep returning to the same themes: repair work, care work, local food, mutual aid, honest infrastructure, and a politics that takes the material conditions of life seriously instead of laundering everything through financial abstractions.
This is one more proof.
A government's first job is not war profits. It is not narrative management. It is not making sure contractors and speculators land softly. Its job is to protect the people and maintain the conditions for dignified life.
Food. Heat. Water. Medicine. Transport. Public order without cruelty. Truth without euphemism.
That is what serious governance looks like.
And if our governing class will not act with that seriousness, then the responsibility falls downward and outward: to states, counties, towns, farms, neighborhoods, congregations, and households. To the people who still know how to repair, store, grow, cook, mend, share, and organize.
That is not the future I would have chosen.
But it is the one increasingly visible from here.
So, friends: prepare.
Not with hysteria.
Not with swagger.
Not with fantasies of rugged individualism.
Prepare like an adult.
Prepare like a neighbor.
Prepare like someone who understands that when systems shake, **the line between hardship and catastrophe is often one stocked shelf, one full tank, one extra prescription refill, one working relationship, one good piece of local information.**
If the worst projections are wrong, you will still be better provisioned, less fragile, and more connected to the people around you.
If they are even half right, you will be very glad you did not wait.

| | Charlie Kirk lived fast. And he lived loud.

He filled arenas. He lit a fire in the next generation on campus.

He confronted lies and spoke truth with boldness.

And he built a movement and a machine that few ever thought possible.

I saw it up close -- _Charlie moved at a pace most couldn 't keep up with. _

But in the middle of all the noise... he made a quiet decision that changed everything.

_**He started observing the Sabbath. **_

Not as a box to check. Not as a religious performance.

_But as an act of obedience. _

As a way of saying, **_" God, You are enough. And because You are enough, I need not carry the weight of a world that was never mine to hold." _**

Every week -- no matter what -- Charlie stopped.

He turned off the noise. He stepped away from the battlefield.

No email. No media. No work.

He gave his full attention fully to God, his wife Erika, and his children.

It was hard at first -- for someone who carried so much.

But over time, it changed him.

And before he was assassinated, he wrote a book about what he had learned...

It's not a culture war manifesto.

It's a call to stop.

To rest. To breathe. To return to God.

**Because Charlie believed America hadn 't just forgotten truth... It had forgotten trust. **

Trust that the world keeps spinning when you step away.

Trust that God is in control.

Trust that rest is not weakness -- it's worship.

**In _Stop, in the Name of God,_ you'll discover: **

🔥 How Charlie reclaimed the Sabbath in a world built on burnout

🔥 What sacred rest gave back to him -- as a father, husband, and believer

🔥 Why he believed this message could spark revival in a restless generation

Charlie wrote this book because he knew what it meant to nearly lose his peace -- and what it felt like to find it again.

That's the heartbeat of his final message.

| | **Have you heard about the Frontera Fellows program? If you want to join the next generation of Democratic leaders, or know someone who does, share this info and apply now before the application closes. We've extended our deadline to Friday, April 17!** This paid summer fellowship is designed to train the next generation of Democratic leaders right here in El Paso. In partnership with Democracy Summer School and the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, it's designed for high school and college-aged students ready to step into organizing, advocacy, and leadership roles. [APPLY HERE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/129472124/614458044/-1799785547?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDEvMS82MTY0NSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI4MzVlNTU3ZS01MjM4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=GPuabu9_VgG5os4Pg40x1vGBUQlpVKBAXyaFik68YGY=&emci=179019d1-4b38-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=835e557e-5238-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=14565883) Over six weeks, from June 22 through August 7, Fellows will participate in a curriculum I've helped shape while organizing on the ground. That means building real political skills and civic engagement—all the necessary ingredients for a thriving democracy. Fellows also receive a stipend for their participation, so they can earn while they learn. **Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football 's 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. name: Justin Kwasa, LCV
subject: What’s going on with voting by mail?
body:
To view this mail in a browser, copy https://links.messages.lcv.org/servlet/MailView?ms=MTM2MzExNTIS1&r=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&j=MjQ0MDExMjk3MwS2&mt=1&rt=0 into your browser.
Peter, You’ve probably heard about Trump’s latest executive order that tries to limit
voting by mail — an unconstitutional attempt to disenfranchise millions of
voters. This is one in a series of recent, blatant power grabs by the Trump
administration to obstruct free and fair elections, and to keep eligible votes
from being counted. As environmentalists, we have to fight back on this. We care
about what happens to people and our planet, but we can't protect our air, land,
and water without free and fair elections. Period. Here’s 3 fast facts about this executive order: 1. It’s unconstitutional. States run elections, not presidents.The Constitution makes it crystal clear, the president cannot unilaterally
rewrite the rules for our elections, which are set by state leaders. 2. It directs the Department of Homeland Security to create lists of verified U.S.
citizens that the Attorney General can use to investigate and intimidate voters.Compiled from various, and likely outdated, data sources, this could force
states to hand over our information, including our most private data. It creates
a dangerous pretext to target, harass, and harm Americans. This includes state
and local officials, and states that do not comply may lose federal funds. This
is a clear intimidation tactic. 3. It attempts to position the U.S. Postal Service as a voter suppressor.The USPS is a neutral, nondiscriminatory carrier of the mail. This order would
ban them from mailing ballots to people on the list mentioned above. The Postal
Service’s job is to deliver mail and this action is outside its scope and likely
unconstitutional. Voting by mail is essential for millions of people — and is proven safe, secure,
and trusted by the election administrators across the country. This executive
order is designed to intimidate and disenfranchise large numbers of voters,
including immigrant voters, rural voters, voters of color, Tribal voters, and
voters with disabilities. And the kicker is, Trump himself JUST voted by mail. It’s no surprise that Trump issued this executive order just three days after more than 8 million people around the country took to the streets for No Kings
demonstrations, opposing him and his harmful policies. Trump is desperate. He knows that our movements are building power, so he’s trying every trick in
the book to block Americans from voting. Just like with the anti-voter SAVE Act https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/X6bzs~ he’s trying to push through Congress, Trump is hoping to control election
outcomes so he and his MAGA cronies stay in power. But that’s not how our
country or Constitution works, and our movement won’t let that happen. LCV’s work protecting free and fair elections is integral to protecting our
climate, air, water, and Earth. The 2026 midterms are right around the corner,
and we’re working with our state affiliates to mobilize voters, build grassroots
power, and elect and protect pro-climate, pro-democracy leaders in November. Our movement is already gaining back ground with recent redistricting and
primary election wins in key states. And you better believe we’ll be getting our
votes in this fall — whether by mail or in person at the ballot box. With the sustained commitment of members like you, we canprotect our democracy and environment from further harm. Please consider
supporting LCV with a donation today. SUPPORT LCV https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/RZbkcR- Thank you for showing up for people and our planet. Justin Kwasa
Director, Democracy Program P.S. Sign the petition to stop Trump’s attacks on free and fair elections! https://links.messages.lcv.org/els/v2/~ This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. If this isn't the best email address at which to reach you,update your contact information https://www.pages08.net/leagueofconservationvoters/forms/ContactInformation?spMailingID=13631152&spUserID=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&spJobID=MjQ0MDExMjk3MwS2&spReportId=MjQ0MDExMjk3MwS2.Click here to unsubscribe https://www.pages08.net/leagueofconservationvoters/forms/Unsubscribe?spMailingID=13631152&spUserID=NjA3MDU0MTAzNTc3S0&spJobID=MjQ0MDExMjk3MwS2&spReportId=MjQ0MDExMjk3MwS2 from our supporter list.Send us any comments, criticisms, or feedback here mailto:feedback@lcv.org?subject=, or just reply to this email! Thanks for your support.

Washington, DC 20005

There was a time when the American presidency demanded at least a passing acquaintance with restraint, reality, and reverence. That time has passed. In its place sits the narcissistic lunatic Donald Trump. Within the span of one week, old man Orange threatened apocalyptic destruction, dabbled in self-righteous deification, and then insisted with a straight face, that what everyone plainly saw was something else.
Let's begin with the obvious: no serious leader speaks casually about annihilating a "whole civilization." But Donald Trump issued that threat on social media so nonchalantly it was as if the obliteration of millions of people would be no more consequential than a missed tee time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b5add259-f12f-4aa4-8508-78e25e208b34?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The tragedy is not that Donald Trump behaves this way--that was always a given--but that a great many citizens have grown so accustomed to the act that they no longer recognize it for what it is: not strength, not leadership, but a gaudy, relentless assault on reason and faith itself. **Peter, all eyes are on Virginia, with the state one week away from an election that will determine a lot about the future of the redistricting crisis.** Unlike the extreme Republican gerrymanders that were negotiated and passed behind closed doors, Virginia is leaving it to its voters to decide if the state will redraw its congressional lines and level the playing field. This ballot initiative is critical to ensuring the will of the people is heard this November — and it could help put an end to the redistricting crisis Republicans started last summer. Here’s how we got here: _**FIRST**_ : President Trump and anti-democracy forces pushed Republican leaders in Texas, North Carolina, and Missouri to enact mid-decade redraws of their congressional maps — to try to hold on to power in the midterm elections. This brazen power grab is what plunged us into a national redistricting nightmare. _**THEN**_ : Democrats and the fair maps movement fought back — and won. Voters in California overwhelmingly supported a redraw to counteract Texas’s gerrymander. Voters in Indiana organized and defeated a Republican effort to pass its own redraw. And now Virginia voters have an opportunity to level the playing field for the midterms. _**NOW**_ : With just a week to go until Virginia’s election, Republicans are afraid of losing out on their unfair and unearned advantage. Backed by a MAGA-aligned dark money group, they’re resorting to dirty tricks and racist misinformation to try to defeat this ballot measure. The NDRC refuses to let Trump and his MAGA allies confuse voters in their desperate attempt to hold onto power. clean_body: What’s at stake in Virginia, how we got here, and how you can help. | Peter, all eyes are on Virginia, with the state one week away from an election that will determine a lot about the future of the redistricting crisis. Unlike the extreme Republican gerrymanders that were negotiated and passed behind closed doors, Virginia is leaving it to its voters to decide if the state will redraw its congressional lines and level the playing field. This ballot initiative is critical to ensuring the will of the people is heard this November — and it could help put an end to the redistricting crisis Republicans started last summer. Here’s how we got here: FIRST : President Trump and anti-democracy forces pushed Republican leaders in Texas, North Carolina, and Missouri to enact mid-decade redraws of their congressional maps — to try to hold on to power in the midterm elections. This brazen power grab is what plunged us into a national redistricting nightmare. THEN : Democrats and the fair maps movement fought back — and won. Voters in California overwhelmingly supported a redraw to counteract Texas’s gerrymander. Voters in Indiana organized and defeated a Republican effort to pass its own redraw. And now Virginia voters have an opportunity to level the playing field for the midterms. NOW : With just a week to go until Virginia’s election, Republicans are afraid of losing out on their unfair and unearned advantage. Backed by a MAGA-aligned dark money group, they’re resorting to dirty tricks and racist misinformation to try to defeat this ballot measure. Patriot,
---
It's Gary Sinise here. You may know me from my roles in movies like Apollo 13 _ _ and The Green Mile or the CBS television series CSI: NY - but it was in 1994 playing the role of Lt. Dan in Forrest Gump that changed my life and inspired my enduring connection to our defenders, veterans, and first responders. I've served as an Honorary Grand Marshal for the National Memorial Day Parade in Washington, D.C. nearly every year since American Veterans Center revived it in 2005. **But I've never been more excited to serve as an Honorary Grand Marshall than I am this year - the year of America's 250****th**** birthday.**

Imagine a judge ordering you to keep your own child out of church. And a state depraved enough to shrug it off with indifference.
That is the reality for Emily Bickford in Cumberland County, Maine, thanks to an order imposed by Portland District Court Judge Jennifer Nofsinger.
She's speaking out now for the first time in a video released through Liberty Counsel, the civil rights advocacy organization that is representing her pro bono.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/78e6cc42-53ed-40bc-adf2-1510e4398ca4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Share The Robinson Report](https://substack..0v9Cujt-PyUBO6M7K8rg224vVTUktup8o3bCkbLAs5U?)
In December 2024, Judge Nofsinger -- appointed to the court by Democrat Gov. Janet Mills -- issued a custody modification. The order granted the father of Bickford's child, Matthew Bradeen, exclusive control over all religious decisions for their 12-year-old daughter.
The judge ruled that the biblical teachings at Calvary Chapel Greater Portland -- one of the fastest growing Christian churches in Maine -- could cause "psychological harm" to the child.
As a result, the order bans Bickford from taking her daughter to her church, reading the Bible with her, or associating with church members unless the father approves.
Liberty Counsel aims to dismantle what it views as an unconstitutional mandate imposed by Nofsinger, who was appointed to the court in 2022 under the name Jennifer Rush.
She took the last name of her partner, Jodi L. Nofsinger, a retired attorney whose biography boasts that she "was also well known for her work on civil rights cases, such as the groundbreaking lawsuit brought on behalf of transgender high school student Nicole Maines of Orono, ME."
Stripped of her fundamental First Amendment rights by the court order, Bickford is fighting back against what she advocates describe as an egregious overreach by the judicial system.
News for people with common sense...
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..W3FD3ZBipOlqTgOoyzRaj4mNs2L2mhJ2lUj4wc58hVQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=194243065)
"Being in church is our whole life," Bickford said. "We just love coming to church."
The prohibition has taken a toll on her family, particularly confusing her daughter, who cannot fathom why the government would bar them from the pews.
"She says, 'I just don't understand why I can't just go to church,'" Bickford recounted. "'If it goes against the Constitution, then why can't I go to church?'"
It is a question that exposes the absurdity of the state's position. While the state government routinely ignores constitutional guardrails, Bickford's case is unique in its brazen disregard for religious liberty.
Carey, who has watched the ordeal unfold and who was even dragged into court to explain Christianity to the menacing judge, noted the toll the court order has taken on her.
"I must say it has been astounding to watch the Lord strengthen Emily through this," Travis said. "Emily has had an unwavering faith, but it has undeniably been difficult for her emotionally and spiritually."
"It has been a bittersweet thing as usually persecution is," Travis said. "It's difficult, but it also allows the body of Christ and the love of Christ to shine through."
The case is currently awaiting a ruling from the Maine Supreme Judicial Court.
The court heard oral arguments in _Bickford v. Bradeen_ on November 13, 2025, and the justices are currently deliberating.
If the state's highest court upholds Judge Jennifer Nofsinger's custody order, Liberty Counsel has publicly stated they will appeal the decision to the U.S. Supreme Court.

Judge Jennifer Nofsinger, a far left judge and LGBTQ activist placed on the court by Gov. Janet Mills (D), imposed the unprecedented order on a member of Calvary Chapel Greater Portland. Apr 14 | | | | | | | | | | | Imagine a judge ordering you to keep your own child out of church. And a state depraved enough to shrug it off with indifference. That is the reality for Emily Bickford in Cumberland County, Maine, thanks to an order imposed by Portland District Court Judge Jennifer Nofsinger. She's speaking out now for the first time in a video released through Liberty Counsel, the civil rights advocacy organization that is representing her pro bono. ? In December 2024, Judge Nofsinger -- appointed to the court by Democrat Gov. Janet Mills -- issued a custody modification. The order granted the father of Bickford's child, Matthew Bradeen, exclusive control over all religious decisions for their 12-year-old daughter. The judge ruled that the biblical teachings at Calvary Chapel Greater Portland -- one of the fastest growing Christian churches in Maine -- could cause "psychological harm" to the child. As a result, the order bans Bickford from taking her daughter to her church, reading the Bible with her, or associating with church members unless the father approves. Liberty Counsel aims to dismantle what it views as an unconstitutional mandate imposed by Nofsinger, who was appointed to the court in 2022 under the name Jennifer Rush. She took the last name of her partner, Jodi L. Nofsinger, a retired attorney whose biography boasts that she "was also well known for her work on civil rights cases, such as the groundbreaking lawsuit brought on behalf of transgender high school student Nicole Maines of Orono, ME." Stripped of her fundamental First Amendment rights by the court order, Bickford is fighting back against what she advocates describe as an egregious overreach by the judicial system. News for people with common sense... "Being in church is our whole life," Bickford said. "We just love coming to church." The prohibition has taken a toll on her family, particularly confusing her daughter, who cannot fathom why the government would bar them from the pews. "She says, 'I just don't understand why I can't just go to church,'" Bickford recounted. "'If it goes against the Constitution, then why can't I go to church?'" It is a question that exposes the absurdity of the state's position. While the state government routinely ignores constitutional guardrails, Bickford's case is unique in its brazen disregard for religious liberty. Carey, who has watched the ordeal unfold and who was even dragged into court to explain Christianity to the menacing judge, noted the toll the court order has taken on her. "I must say it has been astounding to watch the Lord strengthen Emily through this," Travis said. "Emily has had an unwavering faith, but it has undeniably been difficult for her emotionally and spiritually." "It has been a bittersweet thing as usually persecution is," Travis said. "It's difficult, but it also allows the body of Christ and the love of Christ to shine through." The case is currently awaiting a ruling from the Maine Supreme Judicial Court. The court heard oral arguments in Bickford v. Bradeen on November 13, 2025, and the justices are currently deliberating. If the state's highest court upholds Judge Jennifer Nofsinger's custody order, Liberty Counsel has publicly stated they will appeal the decision to the U.S. Supreme Court. * You 're receiving The Robinson Report for free. I'm talking about real results. The most conservative judges ever appointed to the bench happened during my chairmanship. Remember when the Left tried to destroy Justice Brett Kavanaugh? I defended him. When the radicals on the Left sought to block the confirmation of Justice Amy Coney Barrett, I was the Chairman. She was confirmed. This is my record, Fellow American. But here's the truth Democrats won't say out loud: Democrats are targeting me because they know exactly what I will do when I am Chairman again. They know I will get back to work confirming judges. They know I won't back down. And they are determined to take the Senate majority to stop it all, undoing everything we've accomplished with President Trump. I am not going to let that happen without a fight. Don't let the Left get what they want. Don't let the Left take the courts. Don't let them erase our progress.
